title: Open WebUI realtime auth -- T1550 Redis-revoked JWT still authenticates Socket.IO and terminal WebSocket connections
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-59219 (GHSA-855v-hq7w-jmjw,
CVSS 7.1 HIGH -- corrected 2026-09-04 via live GHSA lookup, the rule's
original authoring understated this score), affecting Open WebUI's
realtime authentication surfaces from v0.9.0 until v0.10.0, when Redis
is configured.

HTTP auth (`get_current_user` in `utils/auth.py`) rejects a JWT
whose `jti` is recorded as revoked in Redis (via sign-out or OIDC
back-channel logout) with 401. The realtime authentication paths --
Socket.IO `connect`, `user-join`, `join-channels`, `join-note` in
`socket/main.py`, and the terminal WebSocket first-message auth in
`terminals.py` -- validate the token with `decode_token()` only,
which checks signature and expiry but never consults the Redis
revocation keys. A token revoked by the exact action meant to kill
it -- the user signing out, or the identity provider's back-channel
logout -- therefore continues to authenticate NEW realtime
connections: it can join the victim's user/channel/note rooms,
receive realtime messages and collaborative-note updates, and pass
terminal WebSocket auth where terminal servers are configured. HTTP
remains correctly protected throughout.

Detection logic flags a Socket.IO or terminal-WebSocket connection
authenticated with a JWT `jti` that a `POST /api/v1/auths/signout`
or OIDC back-channel logout event for the same `jti` preceded -- the
exact revoked-but-still-authenticating sequence this advisory
describes.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing the exact functions, source files, and a
reporter proof-of-concept demonstrating HTTP 401 alongside a
successful realtime connection on the same revoked token), fixed in
v0.10.0.
